entries.t: Privacy & How We Protect Your Information
entries.x: What personal information the Run the Room forms collect, why we collect it, and how we protect it.
entries.w: privacy & how we protect your information what personal information the run the room forms collect, why we collect it, and how we protect it. run the room is produced by professional development inc. producer: charles mayfield. this page explains what personal information our forms collect, why, and how we protect it. through our internship application form: your name and email, school and program, a résumé and optional writing sample, a copy of your state-issued id (driver's license or state id card). a state-issued id shows your full legal name, photograph, date of birth, home address, id number, and physical description; uploading a copy gives us all of that information. we use the copy only to verify age and identity (see id copies, below). through our call-request form: your name, email, phone number, organization and role (optional), what you'd like to discuss, your best times and time zone, and any extra notes you choose to add. google forms requires you to sign in to a google account to upload files, and google records the name, email address, and profile photo of the account you use together with your submission. who may apply: all internship participants must be 18 years of age or older and their own legal guardian — that is, not subject to a guardianship or conservatorship. direct applications are open to applicants age 18 or older only; the form asks whether you are 18 or older and collects nothing from anyone who is not. adult students (18 or older) may also be referred by their school, in which case their school transmits their application materials to us and certifies that the participant meets the program's eligibility requirements. schools do not send us copies of id in the school channel — the school verifies the student's age itself. we do not collect information from anyone under 18. privacy.html privacy.html

entries.t: Starting From Zero: What a Business Actually Is
entries.x: Starting From Zero opens Run the Room at the true beginning: what a business actually is. Alex and Jordan define a business as an organized answer to somebody else's problem, offered in exchange for money, with the machinery to keep that exchange going — then…
entries.w: starting from zero: what a business actually is starting from zero opens run the room at the true beginning: what a business actually is. alex and jordan define a business as an organized answer to somebody else's problem, offered in exchange for money, with the machinery to keep that exchange going — then test that definition against peter drucker's 1954 claim that the purpose of a business is to create a customer, the three legs of offer, customers, and money, bureau of labor statistics survival data, cash-flow research, and four common impostors: a hobby, a job you buy yourself, an audience, and a product without a system. new episodes every sunday. run the room builds business from the very beginning — foundations first, one step each week. sources: - peter drucker, the practice of management (1954), p. 37: "there is only one valid definition of business purpose: to create a customer" — https://en.wikiquote.org/w/index.php?title=peter_drucker&oldid=2975895 - u.s. small business administration, launch your business guide (structure, registration, tax ids, licenses): https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business - u.s. small business administration, choose a business structure (updated march 7, 2025): https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/launch-your-business/choose-business-structure - bureau of labor statistics, business employment dynamics establishment survival through march 2025 (77.9% year 1, 51.4% at 5 years for the 2020 cohort, 34.7% at 10 years for the 2015 cohort), summarized at: https://startbusinessbystate.com/business-survival-rates-by-state/ - score / u.s. bank study cited on cash flow and small business failure (about 82% tied to poor cash flow management), and federal reserve 2026 report on employer firms based on the 2025 small business credit survey: https://www.oneparkfinancial.com/blog/why-82-percent-of-small-businesses-fail-because-of-cash-flow to verify items without a stable url: search the bureau of labor statistics site for business employment dynamics table 7 establishment age and survival, and search the federal reserve site for the 2026 report on employer firms, small business credit survey.
